claim.claim-text: generating, using an event camera comprising a plurality of light sensors at a plurality of respective locations, a plurality of event messages, each of the plurality of event messages being generated in response to a particular light sensor detecting a change in intensity of light and indicating a particular location of the particular light sensor; and determining an eye tracking characteristic of a user based on the plurality of event messages.
2. The method of claim 1, wherein each of the plurality of event messages further indicates a polarity of the change in intensity of light.
3. The method of claims 1 or 2, wherein each of the plurality of event messages further indicates a time at which the change in intensity of light was detected.

4. The method of any of claims 1-3, wherein each of the plurality of event messages are generated in response to a particular light sensor detecting at least a threshold amount of change in intensity of light.
5. The method of any of claims 1-4, wherein the particular location is indicated by a pixel coordinate.
6. The method of any of claims 1-5, wherein determining the eye tracking characteristic includes detecting a pupil of an eye of the user.
7. The method of claim 6, wherein detecting the pupil includes:
8. The method of any of claims 1-7, wherein determining the eye tracking characteristic includes tracking a pupil of an eye of the user.
9. The method of claim 8, wherein tracking the pupil of the eye of the user includes:
locating one or more high-contrast edges based on the event messages from the event camera; and fitting a new ellipse based on the one or more high-contrast edges and a prior ellipse.
10. The method of any of claims 1-9, wherein determining the eye tracking characteristic includes detecting one or more glints reflected from an eye of the user.

11. The method of claim 10, wherein detecting the one or more glints is based on event messages that indicate an increase in intensity of light without being based on event messages that indicate a decrease in intensity of light.

12. The method of claim 10, wherein detecting the one or more glints is based on event messages that indicate a decrease in intensity of light without being based on event messages that indicate an increase in intensity of light.
13. The method of any of claims 1-12, wherein the eye tracking characteristic includes a gaze direction.

14. The method of any of claims 1-13, wherein the event camera is different from a frame camera that generates one or more video frames, and wherein the light intensity data does not include information regarding the one or more video frames.

an event camera comprising a plurality of light sensors at a plurality of respective locations, the event camera to generate, in response to particular light sensor detecting a change in intensity of light, an event message indicating a particular location of the particular light sensor; and an eye tracker to receive event messages from the event camera and determine an eye tracking characteristic of a user based on the event messages.
